title: 2.1.1 Libraries and JSCAD Introduction
description: Learn what a software library is, import @jscad/modeling, and write your first 3D program.

steps.title: Import the library
steps.instructions: Use `require('@jscad/modeling')` to import the JSCAD library and destructure the `primitives` module.
hints: The syntax is: const { primitives } = require('@jscad/modeling')
Destructuring pulls out just the tools you need from the library.

steps.title: Write the main() function
steps.instructions: Create a function called `main` that returns a shape. Every JSCAD program needs this function as its entry point.
hints: function main() { return /* a shape here */; }
main() must return a geometry or an array of geometries.

steps.title: Return a cube
steps.instructions: Inside `main()`, use `primitives.cube({ size: 10 })` to create your first 3D shape. Click Run to see it.
hints: primitives.cube() creates a cube. The size property controls how big it is.
Try changing size to 20 or 5 and clicking Run again.

steps.title: Export your main function
steps.instructions: Add `module.exports = { main }` at the bottom so JSCAD knows which function to call.
hints: This line tells the system: 'my main function is the entry point.'
Without this, JSCAD won't know how to run your code.

steps.title: Experiment with other shapes
steps.instructions: Try `primitives.sphere({ radius: 8 })` or `primitives.cylinder({ radius: 5, height: 15 })`. Import the `transforms` module and use `transforms.translate([10, 0, 0], shape)` to move shapes.
